newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen stagnant amid dearth of incentives.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen stagnant amid dearth of incentives.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were pinned within two-tick trading ranges on Wednesday as a lack of fresh incentives and holidays in Singapore and Japan earlier in the week severely limited participation.

"The interest rate products are having a problem because the majority of traders believe the BOJ (Bank of Japan) is not going to raise rates. So they're not taking any aggressive positions," said a Japanese bank dealer.
He said Euroyen futures showed limited upside potential, but added that players were not prepared to sell them either, keeping activity confined to a tight band.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.38 at 1120 GMT against its IMM close at 99.37 on volume of 4,000 lots. December was at 99.26 unchanged against the IMM on 2,450 lots.

The dealer said September was still the lead month on SIMEX in terms of volume because local players were waiting for a major breakout in the December contract on TIFFE before trading it actively on the Singapore exchange.
Japanese government bond futures for March ended at 126.24 against their previous 126.36.
Dealers said the Nikkei's firm close and the dollar's bullish stance against the yen dampened sentiment at the long end of the yield curve.
Eurodollar futures were scarcely moved in even thinner volume, with September settling at 94.22, unchanged against its IMM close on volume of 3,725 lots.
Dealers said interest would be focused on the U.S. Producer Price Index for January, due to be released on Friday.
